newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to include non-tax revenues in budget.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to include non-tax revenues in budget.

text.p: The Indonesian government had presented a bill at the House of Representatives which stipulates that the government's non-tax revenues must be accounted for in the annual state budget, The Jakarta Post daily reported on Tuesday.

"All government institutions will be obliged to transfer any non-tax revenues they collect to the state treasury as an effort to improve budgetary discipline," newspaper quoted Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad as saying when presented the bill on Monday.
Mar'ie said the draft legislation covers all government income from sources other than taxes such as licensing fees, royalties, rents and investment income from state assets.
Non-tax revenues collected by the government currently do not go into the government's account at the Ministry of Finance, but to government departments or institutions.

Indonesia has projected that non-tax receipts will rise 12 percent to 8.2 trillion rupiah in the 1997/98 fiscal year beginning in April, from 7.26 trillion rupiah in the current fiscal year, the daily reported.
